Timeline::years_between¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::years_between(const Timeline& other) const

Count Completed Calendar-Year Anniversaries¶

years_between() returns the signed number of complete calendar years from the scalar receiver to scalar other. It is an anniversary calculation, not elapsed seconds divided by 365 days. The date, local clock, and timezone all participate in deciding whether the final anniversary has occurred.

The method uses the same calendar clamping as add_years(). That matters for a leap-day receiver: its anniversary in a non-leap year is 28 February at the same local time. The result is a native std::int64_t, making the method appropriate for scalar age, tenure, and completed-cycle logic.

Example: A Leap-Day Anniversary Clamps To February 28¶

const auto leap = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:00:00Z");
const auto anniversary = pluss::timeline::make("2025-02-28T12:00:00Z");
const auto one_second_early =
    pluss::timeline::make("2025-02-28T11:59:59Z");

std::cout << "complete=" << leap.years_between(anniversary) << '\n'
          << "incomplete=" << leap.years_between(one_second_early) << '\n';

Output¶

complete=1
incomplete=0

The date alone is insufficient. At 11:59:59 the clamped anniversary remains one second away, so no complete year is counted.

Example: Reverse Intervals Are Symmetric¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:00:00Z");
const auto end = pluss::timeline::make("2025-02-28T12:00:00Z");

std::cout << start.years_between(end) << '\n'
          << end.years_between(start) << '\n';

Output¶

1
-1

The method computes the complete-unit magnitude chronologically and applies the direction afterward. This avoids the asymmetric floor behavior that would turn an incomplete reverse interval into an extra negative year.

Example: Reject An Ambiguous Calendar Frame¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");

try {
  (void)utc.years_between(local);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected

Calendar distances require matching timezone names even when two values denote the same instant. Explicit conversion makes the intended local calendar clear. Both operands must also be scalar and neither may be NaT.

Choosing The Related Operation¶

Use years_between() for one signed scalar count under clamped-anniversary semantics. Use add_years() to construct the anniversary. Use span() for arrays, broadcasting, unsigned magnitudes, boundary counts, or explicit month-end anchoring. The method is constant-time and does not mutate either operand.

See Also¶

  • months_between: count complete calendar months.

  • add_years: move by calendar years.

  • span: configure elementwise calendar spans.
